cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the church of God in Corinth. He's just told them we all must appear before the judgment seat of Christ. So now Paul says, "we know what it means to fear the Lord."

cards.question: Paul knows what it means to fear the Lord. So what does he try to do with people?

cards.text: Paul says what he is, is clear to God, and he hopes it's clear to the Corinthians' conscience too. Then he adds that he's NOT commending himself to them again. No sir. Not AGAIN.

cards.question: Instead, Paul gives the Corinthians a reason to be proud of him, so they can answer those who take pride in ___ rather than in the heart.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "If we are out of our mind, it is for God." Out of your mind for God? Friend, I talk to my oven every morning, and NOBODY has ever accused me of a sound mind.

cards.question: Paul says if we are out of our mind, it is for God. But if we are of sound mind, who is it for?
Paul says what compels him is his fear of what people think.

cards.text: Here's what's really driving him: Christ's love compels him. Paul is convinced that "One died for all, therefore all died."

cards.question: Christ died for all, so that those who live should no longer live for ___ but for Him who died for them and was raised again.

cards.text: So from now on, Paul says, we regard no one according to the flesh. From NOW on, friend. That's a line drawn right through the flour.

cards.question: Paul says that at one time, even Christ was regarded according to the flesh.

cards.text: Then comes the big one: "Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation." Friend, I went into a junk drawer blurry and came out SHARP, so this verse hits me right in the handle.

cards.question: If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. So what does Paul say about the old?

cards.text: All this is from God, Paul says, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ. And God doesn't stop there. He hands us a JOB: the ministry of reconciliation.

cards.question: God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men's ___ against them.
God keeps the message of reconciliation to Himself and commits it to no one.
Paul says God has committed the message of reconciliation to us. So what does Paul say we are?

cards.text: Paul says it's "as though God were making His appeal through us." Friend, if God made an appeal through ME, I'd be so nervous my mustache would wave at everybody in the room.

cards.question: Paul pleads with them on behalf of Christ: Be ___ to God.

cards.text: Then Paul packs the whole message into one verse. "God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf," he writes. Read that one slow, friend.

cards.question: God made the One who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf. Why?

answers.text: So in Him we might become the righteousness of God
So we would never have to face hard times again
So the law of Moses could finally be thrown out

cards.text: Paul calls them God's fellow workers. Fellow workers with GOD? Friend, I've got "cookie stamper" on my résumé and I thought THAT was impressive.

cards.question: As God's fellow workers, what does Paul urge the Corinthians not to do with God's grace?

cards.text: Then Paul quotes God's words from Isaiah 49:8: "In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you."

cards.question: Paul says the day of salvation is still a long way off.

cards.text: Not someday. Not after you hit snooze five more times. "Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!"

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 quotes "we know what it means to fear the Lord.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 5 quotes "If we are out of our mind, it is for God.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage without references. It says Paul has just told them we all must appear before the judgment seat of Christ (2 Corinthians 5:10) and that the letter goes to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). The card cites only 2 Corinthians 5:11.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This card says God 'hands us a JOB: the ministry of reconciliation' (5:18). Two cards later, card 3 asks the baker to mark true or false whether God keeps the message of reconciliation to Himself and commits it to no one. Card 1 has already given that answer away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The right answer ('So in Him we might become the righteousness of God') sounds like the Bible. The wrong answers sound modern and casual ('never have to face hard times again', 'could finally be thrown out'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card says 'Paul calls them God's fellow workers,' meaning the Corinthians. In 2 Corinthians 6:1 ('As God's fellow workers, then, we urge you'), the fellow workers are Paul and those with him, not the Corinthians. The joke on this card is built on that misreading.

rule.text: He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Try to earn it' is something a baker could argue Paul also urges against, since grace is not earned (for example Ephesians 2:8-9). That makes it arguably right.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
